0.long_answer: Babesiosis is a disease caused by infection with Babesia parasites, most commonly Babesia microti in the United States. A key microscopic feature used to diagnose babesiosis is the observation of red blood cell inclusions that form a characteristic Maltese cross pattern. This pattern, which can be described as four V-shaped quadrilaterals converging at right angles, results from the tetrad arrangement of the parasites within the red blood cell. This distinctive morphology is a helpful diagnostic clue when assessing patients with symptoms of babesiosis, especially in endemic regions.
